transcript.text: Hi, we've just had a Bosch KGN36VLEAG delivered last week and it makes a gurgling, bubbling sound like water running, plus a click every so often and a crack noise at night. Is it faulty? It's driving my husband mad.

It is probably not faulty. The sounds you are describing are completely normal for a modern fridge-freezer like your Bosch KGN36VLEAG. The gurgling and bubbling noise is the sound of refrigerant (the cooling fluid) flowing through the pipes inside the walls of the appliance as it changes from liquid to gas. This can sound exactly like water running in the pipes, even though no water is moving there. The clicking you hear occasionally is likely the compressor starting up or shutting down, which happens several times a day. The cracking noise at night is also normal. It is caused by the plastic interior panels and insulation expanding and contracting as the temperature inside changes slightly during the cooling cycle. This is often more noticeable in quiet rooms at night. You do not need to do anything. The only time these sounds indicate a problem is if they are accompanied by the fridge failing to keep food cold, or if you see an oily residue on the floor (which would suggest a leak). Since your appliance was just delivered and presumably cooling fine, you can rest easy.

candidates: Normal refrigerant flow and thermal expansion (high)

reading.symptom: gurgling, bubbling sound like water running, click every so often, crack noise at night

plan: They asked: "Is it faulty?" - answer that first.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Bosch; model KGN36VLEAG.
The fault they reported is: "gurgling, bubbling sound like water running, click every so often, crack noise at night". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
